public_rationale: Independent evidence supports continuing unreliability, including hallucinations. It also documents progress. Neither finding settles the stronger assertion that none of Marcus's warnings had been properly addressed. That requires a complete inventory and a defensible resolution criterion for each problem. The evidence does not justify replacing his universal claim with the narrower claim that some problems persisted.
limitations: The supporting experiment is a difficult benchmark, not a representative sample of all generative-AI use.
The research publication dates identify reported model snapshots; individual evaluation-run dates were not established.
Failure to verify the universal claim is not evidence that a general solution existed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI has been inherently unreliable from the start and none of the problems Marcus warned about in the last five years has been properly solved.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI has been inherently unreliable from the start; none of the problems that I warned about over the last half decade has been properly solved.
statement.document_title: Turns out Generative AI was a scam

our_interpretation: Read reliability as dependable factual and reasoning performance across ordinary intended uses, rather than perfect performance on every possible input.
Read properly solved as a durable general solution to a problem class, rather than an improvement on selected examples.
Use 2021-02-23 through publication for the explicit five-year retrospective. The earlier starting point implied by from the start is unspecified.
Retain the universal commitment: evidence that some problems persist does not establish that none has been solved.
criteria.support_condition: Identify the substantive problems Marcus warned about during the stated period and show independently that every identified problem remained unresolved at publication, with historical evidence for persistent unreliability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Show that at least one identified problem had a durable general solution by publication, or establish reliable performance that directly contradicts the claimed inherent limitation.

evidence.excerpt: The toxicity problem, for example, is never going to be solved.
evidence.locator: Interview transcript, Marcus's answer about GPT-3 and robustness
evidence.publisher: Carnegie Council for Ethics in International Affairs
evidence.explanation: This establishes toxicity as one warning within the retrospective period. Marcus's statement is not evidence that the warning was correct.
The model snapshot reported before publication supports continued factual unreliability. It establishes persistence of one problem, not the universal claim about every earlier warning.
The same research documents improvements. These caution against reading Marcus as saying there was no progress, but improvement alone does not establish a general solution.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A complete inventory of the referenced warnings, explicit problem-specific resolution criteria, and independent evaluations of each as of 2026-02-23.
